delete.description:
Hard-delete every recommendation matching the selection, dependents first, and
purge the recommendation agent operations of the resources in scope.

Superuser-only destructive action. Same params and WHERE clause as
GET /selection/preview, so ``matched`` equals the preview's ``meta.total_count``.

At least one of ``resource_types`` / ``action_types`` / ``resource_identifiers``
is required here (the preview does not require it): an unscoped selection is the
account's whole recommendation set, which this endpoint must not be able to
delete. Naming resources alone is a valid scope — it is the narrowest one.

The agent-operation purge is what makes this a clean slate rather than only a
delete: a stale ENDED_NO_RECOMMENDATION / ENDED_FAILURE attempt keeps the
no-result cooldown skipping the resource, and it carries no recommendation FK,
so deleting recommendations alone leaves the resource still skipped on the next
run. **It destroys that attempt history irreversibly** (``agent_operations_deleted``
reports how much), and it covers every resource in scope — including resources
that had no recommendation at all. It is scoped by ``resource_identifiers`` and
``resource_types`` only; a selection scoped by ``action_types`` alone names no
resource and purges nothing.

It also purges the DR-062 ``recommendation_consideration_outcome`` rows of those
resources' bases. Those survive the operation purge on their own — their FK to
the operation is ON DELETE SET NULL — and a watermark-advancing row permanently
suppresses reconsideration of that basis. **Also irreversible**
(``consideration_outcomes_deleted``). Non-zero only where DR-062 has minted
bases, which today is AWS EC2 only.

post.description:
Run evaluations for an explicit batch of Langfuse observations.

Each target observation gets its own ephemeral ``FeedbackSignals`` value.

Authorization model
-------------------
Observation IDs are unscoped Langfuse identifiers supplied by the client.
There is **no** ownership check that binds an observation to the caller's
company, cloud account, or business unit.
This is intentional: the endpoint is restricted to ``user:global:super-admin``
users (enforced by ``_require_super_admin`` below), making it a
platform-admin-only global operation.

If this endpoint is ever opened beyond super-admin users, an ownership
validation step (observation → trace → cloud account → company)
must be added before forwarding to ``EvaluationService``.

Operational guardrails
----------------------
* **Timeout**: the eval pipeline is bounded by ``_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS``
  inside ``EvaluationService``; exceeding it returns HTTP 408.
* **Idempotency**: ``EvaluationAgent.write_scores`` uses a deterministic
  ``score_id`` per matched observation+score_name so Langfuse upserts
  rather than duplicates on re-runs.
* **Audit logging**: every accepted call is logged with ``user_id`` and
  observation IDs inside ``EvaluationService`` before any external I/O.
